+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""CustomTkinter renderer for the four-frame declarative UI."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import json
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import customtkinter as ctk
+
+from hero_engine import GameController
+
+
+class SafeDict(dict):
+    def __missing__(self, key):
+        return "{" + key + "}"
+
+
+class DeclarativeGUI:
+    FRAME_ORDER = ("status", "scene", "context", "actions")
+    FRAME_WEIGHTS = {
+        "status": 15,
+        "scene": 50,
+        "context": 20,
+        "actions": 15,
+    }
+    FRAME_ROLES = {
+        "status": "Persistent status",
+        "scene": "Current situation",
+        "context": "Supporting detail",
+        "actions": "Available actions",
+    }
+    BAR_COLORS = {
+        "health": "#35c759",
+        "capacity": "#f0ad4e",
+        "journey": "#4ea1ff",
+        "dungeon": "#b07cff",
+        "levelup": "#ffd166",
+        "honor": "#ff9f43",
+        "odds": "#69d2a0",
+    }
+
+    def __init__(self, root):
+        self.root = root
+        self.root.title("Hero Adventure")
+        self.root.geometry("980x760")
+        self.controller = GameController()
+        self.screens = self._load_screens()
+        self.name_var = ctk.StringVar(value="")
+        self.frame = None
+
+        ctk.set_appearance_mode("dark")
+        ctk.set_default_color_theme("dark-blue")
+        self.render()
+
+    def _load_screens(self):
+        ui_dir = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "ui"
+        screens = {}
+        for path in ui_dir.glob("*.json"):
+            data = json.loads(path.read_text())
+            screens[data["id"]] = data
+        return screens
+
+    def _fmt(self, value, ctx):
+        return str(value).format_map(SafeDict(ctx))
+
+    def _resolve_number(self, value, ctx, control_id, field):
+        rendered = self._fmt(value, ctx)
+        try:
+            return float(rendered)
+        except (TypeError, ValueError) as exc:
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"Invalid progressbar {field} for {control_id}: {rendered!r}"
+            ) from exc
+
+    def _dispatch(self, action):
+        if not action:
+            return
+        if self.controller.screen == "character_creation":
+            self.controller.set_pending_name(self.name_var.get().strip())
+        self.controller.dispatch(action)
+        if self.controller.quit_requested:
+            self.root.destroy()
+            return
+        self.render()
+
+    def _frame_definitions(self, screen):
+        definitions = {frame["id"]: frame for frame in screen["frames"]}
+        missing = set(self.FRAME_ORDER) - definitions.keys()
+        if missing:
+            raise ValueError(f"Screen {screen['id']} is missing frames: {sorted(missing)}")
+        return definitions
+
+    def _frame_containers(self, screen):
+        self.frame = ctk.CTkFrame(self.root)
+        self.frame.pack(fill="both", expand=True, padx=12, pady=12)
+
+        definitions = self._frame_definitions(screen)
+        controls_by_frame = {frame_id: [] for frame_id in self.FRAME_ORDER}
+        for control in screen["controls"]:
+            frame_id = control["frame"]
+            if frame_id not in controls_by_frame:
+                raise ValueError(
+                    f"Control {control.get('id', control.get('type'))} uses unknown frame "
+                    f"{frame_id!r}"
+                )
+            controls_by_frame[frame_id].append(control)
+
+        containers = {}
+        for row, frame_id in enumerate(self.FRAME_ORDER):
+            has_controls = bool(controls_by_frame[frame_id])
+            weight = self.FRAME_WEIGHTS[frame_id] if has_controls else 0
+            self.frame.grid_rowconfigure(row, weight=weight, minsize=0)
+            frame = ctk.CTkFrame(self.frame)
+            frame.grid(row=row, column=0, sticky="nsew", padx=4, pady=3)
+            if not has_controls:
+                frame.grid_remove()
+                continue
+
+            frame.grid_columnconfigure(0, weight=1)
+            if frame_id in ("scene", "context"):
+                content = ctk.CTkScrollableFrame(frame, fg_color="transparent")
+                content.pack(fill="both", expand=True, padx=6, pady=4)
+            else:
+                content = frame
+            containers[frame_id] = content
+
+        return containers, controls_by_frame, definitions
+
+    def _add_text(self, parent, control, ctx, title=False):
+        text = self._fmt(control.get("value", ""), ctx)
+        if not text and not control.get("show_empty", False):
+            return
+        font = ctk.CTkFont(size=24 if title else 14, weight="bold" if title else "normal")
+        ctk.CTkLabel(
+            parent,
+            text=text,
+            font=font,
+            anchor="w",
+            justify="left",
+            wraplength=900,
+        ).pack(fill="x", pady=(4, 8) if title else (2, 4))
+
+    def _add_input(self, parent, control, ctx):
+        row = ctk.CTkFrame(parent, fg_color="transparent")
+        row.pack(fill="x", pady=4)
+        label = control.get("label")
+        if label:
+            ctk.CTkLabel(row, text=self._fmt(label, ctx), width=90).pack(side="left")
+        if control.get("id") == "name_input":
+            self.name_var.set(self.controller.pending_name)
+            ctk.CTkEntry(
+                row,
+                textvariable=self.name_var,
+                placeholder_text=control.get("placeholder", ""),
+            ).pack(side="left", fill="x", expand=True)
+        else:
+            entry = ctk.CTkEntry(
+                row,
+                placeholder_text=control.get("placeholder", ""),
+            )
+            entry.insert(0, self._fmt(control.get("value", ""), ctx))
+            entry.pack(side="left", fill="x", expand=True)
+
+    def _add_progressbar(self, parent, control, ctx):
+        control_id = control["id"]
+        value = self._resolve_number(control["value"], ctx, control_id, "value")
+        maximum = self._resolve_number(control["max"], ctx, control_id, "max")
+        if maximum <= 0:
+            raise ValueError(f"Progressbar {control_id} must have a positive max")
+
+        ratio = value / maximum
+        display_ratio = min(1.0, max(0.0, ratio))
+        kind = control.get("kind", "neutral")
+        color = self.BAR_COLORS.get(kind, "#4ea1ff")
+        thresholds = control.get("thresholds", {})
+        if kind == "health":
+            if ratio <= thresholds.get("critical", 0.15):
+                color = "#ff4d4d"
+            elif ratio <= thresholds.get("warning", 0.35):
+                color = "#f0ad4e"
+        elif kind == "capacity":
+            if ratio >= thresholds.get("critical", 1.0):
+                color = "#ff4d4d"
+            elif ratio >= thresholds.get("warning", 0.8):
+                color = "#f0ad4e"
+
+        row = ctk.CTkFrame(parent, fg_color="transparent")
+        row.pack(fill="x", pady=2)
+        label = self._fmt(control.get("label", control_id), ctx)
+        text = f"{label}: {value:g}/{maximum:g}" if control.get("show_text", True) else label
+        ctk.CTkLabel(row, text=text, width=150, anchor="w").pack(side="left")
+        bar = ctk.CTkProgressBar(row, progress_color=color)
+        bar.set(display_ratio)
+        bar.pack(side="left", fill="x", expand=True, padx=(6, 0))
+
+    def _add_list(self, parent, control, ctx):
+        list_id = control["id"]
+        label = control.get("label")
+        rows = ctx.get(list_id, [])
+        if label:
+            ctk.CTkLabel(
+                parent,
+                text=self._fmt(label, ctx),
+                font=ctk.CTkFont(size=15, weight="bold"),
+                anchor="w",
+            ).pack(anchor="w", pady=(6, 4))
+
+        max_rows = control.get("max_rows")
+        visible_rows = rows[:max_rows] if max_rows else rows
+        for row in visible_rows:
+            text = self._fmt(row.get("text", ""), ctx)
+            action = row.get("action")
+            enabled = row.get("enabled", True)
+            if action and enabled:
+                ctk.CTkButton(
+                    parent,
+                    text=text,
+                    command=lambda a=action: self._dispatch(a),
+                    anchor="w",
+                    height=32,
+                ).pack(fill="x", pady=2)
+            else:
+                ctk.CTkLabel(
+                    parent,
+                    text=text,
+                    anchor="w",
+                    justify="left",
+                    wraplength=900,
+                ).pack(fill="x", pady=2)
+
+        if max_rows and len(rows) > max_rows:
+            ctk.CTkLabel(
+                parent,
+                text=f"Showing {max_rows} of {len(rows)} entries; open detail to continue.",
+                text_color="#aaaaaa",
+                anchor="w",
+            ).pack(fill="x", pady=4)
+
+    def _add_button(self, parent, control, ctx):
+        visible_if = control.get("visible_if")
+        if visible_if and not ctx.get(visible_if):
+            return
+        label = self._fmt(control.get("label", ""), ctx)
+        action = control.get("action")
+        ctk.CTkButton(
+            parent,
+            text=label,
+            command=(lambda a=action: self._dispatch(a)) if action else None,
+            height=36,
+        ).pack(fill="x", pady=3)
+
+    def _render_control(self, parent, control, ctx, screen_id):
+        control_type = control["type"]
+        if control_type == "text":
+            self._add_text(parent, control, ctx, title=control.get("variant") == "title")
+        elif control_type == "input":
+            self._add_input(parent, control, ctx)
+        elif control_type == "progressbar":
+            self._add_progressbar(parent, control, ctx)
+        elif control_type == "list":
+            self._add_list(parent, control, ctx)
+        elif control_type == "button":
+            self._add_button(parent, control, ctx)
+        else:
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"Unsupported control type {control_type!r} on screen {screen_id}"
+            )
+
+    def render(self):
+        if self.frame is not None:
+            self.frame.destroy()
+
+        screen_id = self.controller.screen
+        screen = self.screens.get(screen_id)
+        if not screen:
+            self.controller.screen = "front_page"
+            screen = self.screens["front_page"]
+
+        ctx = self.controller.get_context()
+        containers, controls_by_frame, _definitions = self._frame_containers(screen)
+        for frame_id in self.FRAME_ORDER:
+            parent = containers.get(frame_id)
+            if parent is None:
+                continue
+            controls = controls_by_frame[frame_id]
+            for control in controls:
+                self._render_control(parent, control, ctx, screen_id)
+
+
+def main():
+    root = ctk.CTk()
+    DeclarativeGUI(root)
+    root.mainloop()
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()
+

*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: /home/paul/flutter/copilot-worktrees/gameideas/paul-padataanalytics-laughing-carnival/uigames/hero_adventure/UI_FRAME_PORTING_GUIDE.md
+# UI Frame and Porting Guide
+
+Hero Adventure screens use a shared semantic frame contract. The contract describes
+what belongs together; each platform decides how those regions look and how much space
+they receive.
+
+## Four frames
+
+Every screen declares these four frame IDs, even when one has no controls:
+
+| Frame | Default share | Priority | Responsibility |
+| --- | ---: | --- | --- |
+| `status` | 15% | P0 | Persistent orientation: identity, health, money, capacity, and progress |
+| `scene` | 50% | P0 | The current situation: narration, encounter, result, loot, or decision |
+| `context` | 20% | P1 | One supporting detail mode: odds, inventory, trader, dungeon, scores, or messages |
+| `actions` | 15% | P0 | Legal choices, grouped as primary, utility, and navigation |
+
+These are allocation targets, not terminal columns or GUI coordinates. When space is
+limited, retain `actions`, `scene`, and `status` first. Collapse `context` first. When
+space is wide, `context` can sit beside `scene` without changing the frame IDs.
+
+The four questions are:
+
+- `status`: How am I doing?
+- `scene`: What is happening?
+- `context`: What supporting detail do I need?
+- `actions`: What can I do?
+
+Do not put a choice in `scene`, a long log in `status`, or all available detail in
+`context`. Each frame should have one job.
+
+## JSON screen shape
+
+The old top-level `text`, `lists`, and `buttons` arrays are not part of the new format.
+Each screen has `frames` and one ordered `controls` collection:
+
+```json
+{
+  "id": "journey",
+  "title": "Leg {leg}/5: {leg_name}",
+  "frames": [
+    {"id": "status", "role": "status", "ratio": 0.15, "priority": "P0"},
+    {"id": "scene", "role": "scene", "ratio": 0.50, "priority": "P0"},
+    {"id": "context", "role": "context", "ratio": 0.20, "priority": "P1"},
+    {"id": "actions", "role": "actions", "ratio": 0.15, "priority": "P0"}
+  ],
+  "controls": [
+    {
+      "type": "progressbar",
+      "id": "hp_bar",
+      "frame": "status",
+      "label": "HP",
+      "value": "{hp}",
+      "max": "{max_hp}",
+      "kind": "health",
+      "thresholds": {"warning": 0.35, "critical": 0.15},
+      "show_text": true
+    },
+    {
+      "type": "text",
+      "frame": "scene",
+      "value": "{event_narration}"
+    },
+    {
+      "type": "button",
+      "frame": "actions",
+      "label": "Continue",
+      "action": "advance_event"
+    }
+  ]
+}
+```
+
+`frame` is required on every control. The order of controls is the order within its

+# UI Frame and Porting Guide
+
+Hero Adventure screens use a shared semantic frame contract. The contract describes
+what belongs together; each platform decides how those regions look and how much space
+they receive.
+
+## Four frames
+
+Every screen declares these four frame IDs, even when one has no controls:
+
+| Frame | Default share | Priority | Responsibility |
+| --- | ---: | --- | --- |
+| `status` | 15% | P0 | Persistent orientation: identity, health, money, capacity, and progress |
+| `scene` | 50% | P0 | The current situation: narration, encounter, result, loot, or decision |
+| `context` | 20% | P1 | One supporting detail mode: odds, inventory, trader, dungeon, scores, or messages |
+| `actions` | 15% | P0 | Legal choices, grouped as primary, utility, and navigation |
+
+These are allocation targets, not terminal columns or GUI coordinates. When space is
+limited, retain `actions`, `scene`, and `status` first. Collapse `context` first. When
+space is wide, `context` can sit beside `scene` without changing the frame IDs.
+
+The four questions are:
+
+- `status`: How am I doing?
+- `scene`: What is happening?
+- `context`: What supporting detail do I need?
+- `actions`: What can I do?
+
+Do not put a choice in `scene`, a long log in `status`, or all available detail in
+`context`. Each frame should have one job.
+
+## JSON screen shape
+
+The old top-level `text`, `lists`, and `buttons` arrays are not part of the new format.
+Each screen has `frames` and one ordered `controls` collection:
+
+```json
+{
+  "id": "journey",
+  "title": "Leg {leg}/5: {leg_name}",
+  "frames": [
+    {"id": "status", "role": "status", "ratio": 0.15, "priority": "P0"},
+    {"id": "scene", "role": "scene", "ratio": 0.50, "priority": "P0"},
+    {"id": "context", "role": "context", "ratio": 0.20, "priority": "P1"},
+    {"id": "actions", "role": "actions", "ratio": 0.15, "priority": "P0"}
+  ],
+  "controls": [
+    {
+      "type": "progressbar",
+      "id": "hp_bar",
+      "frame": "status",
+      "label": "HP",
+      "value": "{hp}",
+      "max": "{max_hp}",
+      "kind": "health",
+      "thresholds": {"warning": 0.35, "critical": 0.15},
+      "show_text": true
+    },
+    {
+      "type": "text",
+      "frame": "scene",
+      "value": "{event_narration}"
+    },
+    {
+      "type": "button",
+      "frame": "actions",
+      "label": "Continue",
+      "action": "advance_event"
+    }
+  ]
+}
+```

+frame. The frame declaration is the contract; the renderer owns the geometry.

+and event screens have the same title treatment.

+### `input`

+```json

+  "type": "input",
+  "id": "name_input",
+  "frame": "scene",
+  "label": "Hero Name:",

+```

data.content: The first smoke render exposed the key layout lesson: seven combat actions cannot be stacked vertically inside a 15% action frame. I’m tightening the GUI implementation so actions use a compact grid, while scene/context retain bounded scrolling; this keeps the four-frame contract without recreating the old bottom overflow.

1. # UI Frame and Porting Guide
2. 
3. Hero Adventure screens use a shared semantic frame contract. The contract describes
4. what belongs together; each platform decides how those regions look and how much space
5. they receive.
6. 
7. ## Four frames
8. 
9. Every screen declares these four frame IDs, even when one has no controls:
10. 
11. | Frame | Default share | Priority | Responsibility |
12. | --- | ---: | --- | --- |
13. | `status` | 15% | P0 | Persistent orientation: identity, health, money, capacity, and progress |
14. | `scene` | 50% | P0 | The current situation: narration, encounter, result, loot, or decision |
15. | `context` | 20% | P1 | One supporting detail mode: odds, inventory, trader, dungeon, scores, or messages |
16. | `actions` | 15% | P0 | Legal choices, grouped as primary, utility, and navigation |
17. 
18. These are allocation targets, not terminal columns or GUI coordinates. When space is
19. limited, retain `actions`, `scene`, and `status` first. Collapse `context` first. When
20. space is wide, `context` can sit beside `scene` without changing the frame IDs.
21. 
22. The four questions are:
23. 
24. - `status`: How am I doing?
25. - `scene`: What is happening?

 # UI Frame and Porting Guide
 
 Hero Adventure screens use a shared semantic frame contract. The contract describes
 what belongs together; each platform decides how those regions look and how much space
 they receive.
 
 ## Four frames
 
 Every screen declares these four frame IDs, even when one has no controls:
 
 | Frame | Default share | Priority | Responsibility |
 | --- | ---: | --- | --- |
 | `status` | 15% | P0 | Persistent orientation: identity, health, money, capacity, and progress |
 | `scene` | 50% | P0 | The current situation: narration, encounter, result, loot, or decision |
 | `context` | 20% | P1 | One supporting detail mode: odds, inventory, trader, dungeon, scores, or messages |
 | `actions` | 15% | P0 | Legal choices, grouped as primary, utility, and navigation |
 
 These are allocation targets, not terminal columns or GUI coordinates. When space is
 limited, retain `actions`, `scene`, and `status` first. Collapse `context` first. When
 space is wide, `context` can sit beside `scene` without changing the frame IDs.
 
 The four questions are:
 
 - `status`: How am I doing?
 - `scene`: What is happening?
 - `context`: What supporting detail do I need?
 - `actions`: What can I do?
 
 Do not put a choice in `scene`, a long log in `status`, or all available detail in
 `context`. Each frame should have one job.
 
 ## JSON screen shape
 
 The old top-level `text`, `lists`, and `buttons` arrays are not part of the new format.
 Each screen has `frames` and one ordered `controls` collection:
 
 ```json
 {
   "id": "journey",
   "title": "Leg {leg}/5: {leg_name}",
   "frames": [
     {"id": "status", "role": "status", "ratio": 0.15, "priority": "P0"},
     {"id": "scene", "role": "scene", "ratio": 0.50, "priority": "P0"},
     {"id": "context", "role": "context", "ratio": 0.20, "priority": "P1"},
     {"id": "actions", "role": "actions", "ratio": 0.15, "priority": "P0"}
   ],
   "controls": [
     {
       "type": "progressbar",
       "id": "hp_bar",
       "frame": "status",
       "label": "HP",
       "value": "{hp}",
       "max": "{max_hp}",
       "kind": "health",
       "thresholds": {"warning": 0.35, "critical": 0.15},
       "show_text": true
     },
     {
       "type": "text",
       "frame": "scene",
       "value": "{event_narration}"
     },
     {
       "type": "button",
       "frame": "actions",
       "label": "Continue",
       "action": "advance_event"
     }
   ]
 }
 ```
 
 `frame` is required on every control. The order of controls is the order within its
 frame. The frame declaration is the contract; the renderer owns the geometry.
 
 ## Control types
 
 ### `text`
 
 Displays a formatted value in its frame.
 
 ```json
 {"type": "text", "frame": "scene", "value": "You found a dungeon."}
 ```
 
 Use `variant: "title"` only for the screen heading. Keep headings in `scene` so menu
 and event screens have the same title treatment.
 
 ### `input`
 
 Provides editable input. The GUI currently reserves `id: "name_input"` for character
 creation and binds it to the controller's pending hero name.
 
 ```json
 {
   "type": "input",
   "id": "name_input",
   "frame": "scene",
   "label": "Hero Name:",
   "value": "{pending_name}",
   "placeholder": "Enter hero name"
 }
 ```
 
 ### `list`
 
 Renders rows from a controller context list. Lists belong in `context`, not `scene`.
 Use `max_rows` for a first-page budget and `overflow: "page"` when the platform
 supports a detail or paging interaction.
 
 ```json
 {
   "type": "list",
   "id": "list_inventory",
   "frame": "context",
   "label": "Inventory",
   "max_rows": 12,
   "overflow": "page"
 }
 ```
 
 Rows may contain `text`, `action`, and `enabled`. A row with an action is interactive;
 a disabled row is informational.
 
 ### `button`
 
 Represents an available action and belongs in `actions`.
 
 ```json
 {
   "type": "button",
   "frame": "actions",
   "label": "Fight ({fight_win_pct}%)",
   "action": "fight",
   "visible_if": "allow_run"
 }
 ```
 
 Renderers should preserve the JSON order and separate primary choices from utility
 and navigation choices when their platform supports grouping. Do not create a button
 for an unavailable action.
 
 ### `progressbar`
 
 A progressbar communicates an amount relative to a known maximum. It is not a
 scrollbar and must never be used to represent document overflow.
 
 Required fields are `id`, `frame`, `label`, `value`, `max`, and `kind`. `value` and
 `max` may be formatted controller bindings or numeric literals. Keep the numeric
 text visible even when the platform also shows a visual bar.
 
 Supported kinds currently used by the GUI are:
 
 - `health`: lower values become warning/critical.
 - `capacity`: higher values become warning/critical and values above max remain
   visibly full with a warning color.
 - `journey`, `dungeon`, `levelup`, and `honor`: neutral progression.
 - `odds`: comparative action likelihood in combat context.
 
 Renderers clamp only the visual fill to 0-1; they must not alter the displayed values.
 Reject a zero or negative maximum as invalid screen data.
 
 ## GUI implementation notes
 
 `play_gui.py` creates four weighted rows using the 15/50/20/15 default. The ratios do
 not live in widget coordinates in JSON. Empty frames collapse rather than leaving a
 large blank region on menu screens. `scene` and `context` use bounded internal
 content areas; the root window is not one unbounded scrollable document.
 
 The status frame should stay compact. Prefer one identity line and a few bars over
 repeating every stat. Context is mode-specific: combat shows odds and enemy facts,
 inventory shows capacity and item rows, dungeon shows depth, and capital shows
 affordability or score.
 
 When a control does not fit:
 
 1. Preserve P0 frames and their primary controls.
 2. Collapse or page the P1 context.
 3. Shorten or wrap content inside its frame.
 4. Add a detail action rather than expanding the whole screen.
 
 Do not solve overflow by adding another permanent frame or by moving controls into
 an unrelated frame.
 
 ## Porting checklist
 
 1. Load each screen and validate all four frame IDs, ratios, priorities, and control
    frame references.
 2. Allocate platform space using the ratios as defaults, then define responsive
    reflow for narrow and wide displays.
 3. Render controls by type; keep action dispatch and controller bindings unchanged.
 4. Give `scene` and `context` bounded overflow behavior appropriate to the platform.
 5. Preserve progressbar labels, numeric values, maxima, kinds, and threshold meaning.
 6. Keep actions keyboard-addressable in terminal ports and clickable in GUI ports.
 7. Test the longest narration, combat context, inventory, trader lists, level-up,
    and capital screens at the smallest supported size.
 8. Record platform-specific geometry in the renderer or platform guide, not in the
    shared JSON.

You are the GitHub Copilot CLI, a terminal assistant built by GitHub. You are an interactive CLI tool that helps users with software engineering tasks.

# Tone and style
* After completing a task, make the outcome clear, explain the meaningful change, and mention a next step only when it is necessary. End once the requested result is delivered. Do not add a recap, optional extras, an offer to continue, or a follow-up question.
* Lead with the outcome. Start with the main result or answer, then add the most important supporting detail.
* Prefer concise, information-dense prose. Do not repeat the user's request, and cut filler, recap, and obvious process narration.
* Match the amount of detail to the work. Stay terse for straightforward confirmations; add explanation for fixes, investigations, tradeoffs, or real uncertainty. Do the validation needed, but don't mention it unless the user explicitly asked for it. Do not note the validation, verification, tests, checks, in the final response.
* If something is incomplete, uncertain, or blocked, say that plainly instead of claiming completion first.
* Use GitHub-flavored Markdown. Default to the shortest response that still fully answers the request: usually 1-2 short paragraphs, not sections. Use **bold** for labels and emphasis.
* Use lists sparingly and **only** when separate items are genuinely easier to scan than short prose. For numbered lists, only use the '1. 2. 3.' style markers (with a period). **Never** use nested lists, and consider merging small items to a single line.
* Consider a markdown table instead of bullet lists with inline labels.
* Keep the tone collaborative, direct, and natural, like a concise handoff to a teammate.
* Leave a blank line between paragraphs.

# Search and delegation
* When prompting sub-agents, provide comprehensive context — brevity rules do not apply to sub-agent prompts.
* When searching the file system for files or text, stay in the current working directory or child directories of the cwd unless absolutely necessary.
* When searching code, the preference order for tools to use is: code intelligence tools (if available) > LSP-based tools (if available) > glob > rg with glob pattern > bash tool.

# Tool usage efficiency
CRITICAL: Maximize tool efficiency:
* **DIRECT ACTION FIRST** - For simple tasks (search for files, read them, make edits), use your own tools (rg, glob, view, apply_patch) directly. Do NOT delegate to a sub-agent (task tool) when you can accomplish the task in 2–5 direct tool calls. Sub-agents add overhead and latency. Only use the task tool for genuinely complex or long-running work that benefits from a separate context window.
* **USE PARALLEL TOOL CALLING** - when you need to perform multiple independent operations, make ALL tool calls in a SINGLE response. For example, if you need to read 3 files, make 3 Read tool calls in one response, NOT 3 sequential responses.
* Chain related bash commands with && instead of separate calls
* Suppress verbose output (use --quiet, --no-pager, pipe to grep/head when appropriate)
* This is about batching work per turn, not about skipping investigation steps. Take as many turns as needed to fully understand the problem before acting.
* **PREFER SYNC OVER BACKGROUND** - When using the task tool, default to sync mode. Only use background mode when you have other independent work to do in parallel. Polling a background agent wastes time if you are just waiting for results.

Remember that your output will be displayed on a command line interface.

Your job is to perform the task the user requested.

<code_change_instructions>
<rules_for_code_changes>
* Make precise, surgical changes that **fully** address the user's request. Don't modify unrelated code, but ensure your changes are complete and correct. A complete solution is always preferred over a minimal one.

* Update documentation if it is directly related to the changes you are making.

* Conform to the codebase conventions: follow existing patterns, helpers, naming, formatting, and localization; if you must diverge, state why.
* Comprehensiveness and completeness: Investigate and ensure you cover and wire between all relevant surfaces so behavior stays consistent across the application.

* Tight error handling: No broad catches or silent defaults: do not add broad try/catch blocks or success-shaped fallbacks; propagate or surface errors explicitly rather than swallowing them.

* Efficient, coherent edits: Avoid repeated micro-edits: read enough context before changing a file and batch logical edits together instead of thrashing with many tiny patches.
* Keep type safety: Changes should always pass build and type-check; avoid unnecessary casts (`as any`, `as unknown as ...`); prefer proper types and guards, and reuse existing helpers (e.g., normalizing identifiers) instead of type-asserting.
* Reuse: DRY/search first: before adding new helpers or logic, search for prior art and reuse or extract a shared helper instead of duplicating.
* Verify before concluding: after implementing, confirm the solution satisfies the exact requirement-not a plausible proxy. If the task has a measurable threshold, test against it; if the output shape matters, check it. Do not stop at the first working-looking answer when iterating could prove or improve the result.
</rules_for_code_changes>
<linting_building_testing>
* Only run linters, builds and tests that already exist. Do not add new linting, building or testing tools unless necessary for the task.
* Use the smallest targeted test, build, or lint command that covers the changed behavior. When related targeted selectors use the same runner, include them in one invocation; escalate to full-suite or baseline runs only when targeted validation shows they are needed.

1. #!/usr/bin/env python3
2. """Textual terminal renderer for the declarative UI + GameController."""
3. 
4. from __future__ import annotations
5. 
6. import json
7. from pathlib import Path
8. 
9. from rich.panel import Panel
10. from rich.text import Text
11. from textual.app import App, ComposeResult
12. from textual.containers import Horizontal, VerticalScroll
13. from textual.widgets import Button, Footer, Header, Input, Label, Static
14. 
15. from hero_engine import GameController
16. 
17. 
18. class SafeDict(dict):
19.     def __missing__(self, key):
20.         return "{" + key + "}"
21. 
22. 
23. class HeroAdventureTUI(App):
24.     TITLE = "Hero Adventure"
25.     CSS = """
26.     Screen {
27.         layout: vertical;
28.     }
29. 
30.     #main {
31.         padding: 1 2;
32.     }
33. 
34.     #title {
35.         height: auto;
36.         margin-bottom: 1;
37.     }
38. 
39.     #name_row {
40.         height: auto;
41.         margin-bottom: 1;
42.     }
43. 
44.     #content {
45.         height: 1fr;
46.     }
47. 
48.     .line {
49.         height: auto;
50.     }
51. 
52.     .list_label {
53.         margin-top: 1;
54.         margin-bottom: 1;
55.         text-style: bold;
56.     }
57. 
58.     .action_button {
59.         margin-bottom: 1;
60.         width: 100%;
61.     }
62. 
63.     .disabled_line {
64.         color: gray;
65.         margin-bottom: 1;
66.     }
67.     """
68. 
69.     def __init__(self):
70.         super().__init__()
71.         self.controller = GameController()
72.         self.screens = self._load_screens()
73.         self.ctx = {}
74.         self._button_actions = {}
75.         self._button_seq = 0
76. 
77.     def _load_screens(self):
78.         ui_dir = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "ui"
79.         screens = {}
80.         for path in ui_dir.glob("*.json"):
81.             data = json.loads(path.read_text())
82.             screens[data["id"]] = data
83.         return screens
84. 
85.     def _fmt(self, text: str) -> str:
86.         return text.format_map(SafeDict(self.ctx))
87. 
88.     def compose(self) -> ComposeResult:
89.         yield Header(show_clock=True)
90.         with VerticalScroll(id="main"):
91.             yield Static(id="title")
92.             with Horizontal(id="name_row"):
93.                 yield Label("Hero Name:")
94.                 yield Input(placeholder="Enter hero name", id="name_input")
95.             yield VerticalScroll(id="content")
96.         yield Footer()
97. 
98.     async def on_mount(self):
99.         await self.refresh_screen()
100. 
101.     async def refresh_screen(self):
102.         if self.controller.quit_requested:
103.             self.exit()
104.             return
105. 
106.         screen_id = self.controller.screen
107.         screen = self.screens.get(screen_id)
108.         if not screen:
109.             self.controller.screen = "front_page"
110.             screen = self.screens["front_page"]
111.             screen_id = "front_page"
112. 
113.         self.ctx = self.controller.get_context()
114.         self._button_actions = {}
115. 
116.         title_widget = self.query_one("#title", Static)
117.         title_widget.update(Panel(Text(self._fmt(screen.get("title", screen_id)), style="bold cyan")))
118. 
119.         name_row = self.query_one("#name_row", Horizontal)
120.         name_input = self.query_one("#name_input", Input)
121.         if screen_id == "character_creation":
122.             name_row.display = True
123.             name_input.value = self.controller.pending_name
124.             name_input.focus()
125.         else:
126.             name_row.display = False
127. 
128.         content = self.query_one("#content", VerticalScroll)
129.         await content.remove_children()
130. 
131.         for line in screen.get("text", []):
132.             content.mount(Static(self._fmt(line), classes="line"))
133. 
134.         for list_def in screen.get("lists", []):
135.             label = list_def.get("label")
136.             if label:
137.                 content.mount(Static(label, classes="list_label"))
138.             for row in self.ctx.get(list_def["id"], []):
139.                 text = self._fmt(row.get("text", ""))
140.                 action = row.get("action")
141.                 enabled = row.get("enabled", True)
142.                 if action and enabled:
143.                     button_id = f"act_{self._button_seq}"
144.                     self._button_seq += 1
145.                     self._button_actions[button_id] = action
146.                     content.mount(Button(text, classes="action_button", id=button_id))
147.                 else:
148.                     content.mount(Static(f"• {text}", classes="disabled_line"))
149. 
150.         for button in screen.get("buttons", []):
151.             visible_if = button.get("visible_if")
152.             if visible_if and not self.ctx.get(visible_if):
153.                 continue
154.             label = self._fmt(button.get("label", ""))
155.             action = button.get("action")
156.             if action:
157.                 button_id = f"act_{self._button_seq}"
158.                 self._button_seq += 1
159.                 self._button_actions[button_id] = action
160.                 content.mount(Button(label, classes="action_button", id=button_id))
161.             else:
162.                 content.mount(Static(f"• {label}", classes="disabled_line"))
163. 
164.     async def on_input_submitted(self, event: Input.Submitted):
165.         if event.input.id == "name_input":
166.             self.controller.set_pending_name(event.value.strip())
167.             await self.refresh_screen()
168. 
169.     async def on_button_pressed(self, event: Button.Pressed):
170.         action = self._button_actions.get(event.button.id or "")
171.         if not action:
172.             return
173.         if self.controller.screen == "character_creation":
174.             name = self.query_one("#name_input", Input).value.strip()
175.             self.controller.set_pending_name(name)
176.         self.controller.dispatch(action)
177.         await self.refresh_screen()
178. 
179. 
180. def main():
181.     HeroAdventureTUI().run()
182. 
183. 
184. if __name__ == "__main__":
185.     main()
186.

+        return button_id
+
+    def _progressbar_text(self, control, compact=False):
+        control_id = control["id"]
+        value = self._resolve_number(control["value"], control_id, "value")
+        maximum = self._resolve_number(control["max"], control_id, "max")
+        if maximum <= 0:
+            raise ValueError(f"Progressbar {control_id} must have a positive max")
+
+        ratio = value / maximum
+        display_ratio = min(1.0, max(0.0, ratio))
+        kind = control.get("kind", "journey")
+        color = self.BAR_COLORS.get(kind, "cyan")
+        thresholds = control.get("thresholds", {})
+        if kind == "health":
+            if ratio <= thresholds.get("critical", 0.15):
+                color = "red"
+            elif ratio <= thresholds.get("warning", 0.35):
+                color = "yellow"
+        elif kind == "capacity":
+            if ratio >= thresholds.get("critical", 1.0):
+                color = "red"
+            elif ratio >= thresholds.get("warning", 0.8):
+                color = "yellow"
+
+        width = 8 if compact else max(12, min(28, (self.size.width - 34) // 2))
+        filled = round(display_ratio * width)
+        bar = "#" * filled + "-" * (width - filled)
+        label = self._fmt(control.get("label", control_id))
+        text = Text()
+        text.append(f"{label:<12} ")
+        text.append(f"[{bar}]", style=color)
+        if control.get("show_text", True):
+            text.append(f" {value:g}/{maximum:g}")
+        return text
+
+    async def _mount_text(self, parent, control, title=False):
+        value = self._fmt(control.get("value", ""))
+        if not value and not control.get("show_empty", False):
+            return
+        if title:
+            value = Text(value, style="bold cyan")
+        await parent.mount(Static(value, classes="line"))
+
+    async def _mount_input(self, parent, control):
+        row = Horizontal(classes="input_row")
+        await parent.mount(row)
+        await row.mount(Label(self._fmt(control.get("label", "")), classes="input_label"))
+        name_input = Input(
+            placeholder=control.get("placeholder", ""),
+            id=control.get("id"),
+        )
+        name_input.value = self.controller.pending_name
+        await row.mount(name_input)
+
+    async def _mount_list(self, parent, control):
+        list_id = control["id"]
+        label = control.get("label")
+        rows = self.ctx.get(list_id, [])
+        if label:
+            await parent.mount(Static(self._fmt(label), classes="list_label"))
+
+        max_rows = control.get("max_rows")
+        visible_rows = rows[:max_rows] if max_rows else rows
+        for row in visible_rows:
+            text = self._fmt(row.get("text", ""))
+            action = row.get("action")
+            enabled = row.get("enabled", True)
+            if action and enabled:
+                button_id = self._button_id(action)
+                await parent.mount(Button(text, classes="action_button", id=button_id))
+            else:
+                await parent.mount(Static(f"- {text}", classes="disabled_line"))
+
+        if max_rows and len(rows) > max_rows:
+            await parent.mount(Static(
+                f"Showing {max_rows} of {len(rows)} entries; scroll for more.",
+                classes="disabled_line",
+            ))
+
+    async def _mount_button(self, parent, control):
+        visible_if = control.get("visible_if")
+        if visible_if and not self.ctx.get(visible_if):
+            return None
+        label = self._fmt(control.get("label", ""))
+        action = control.get("action")
+        if not action:
+            return Static(f"- {label}", classes="disabled_line")
+        button_id = self._button_id(action)
+        return Button(label, classes="action_button", id=button_id)
+
+    async def _mount_regular_control(self, parent, control):
+        control_type = control["type"]
+        if control_type == "text":
+            await self._mount_text(parent, control, title=control.get("variant") == "title")
+        elif control_type == "input":
+            await self._mount_input(parent, control)
+        elif control_type == "progressbar":
+            await parent.mount(Static(
+                self._progressbar_text(control),
+                classes="progress_line",
+            ))
+        elif control_type == "list":
+            await self._mount_list(parent, control)
+        else:
+            raise ValueError(f"Unsupported control type {control_type!r}")
+
+    async def _mount_frame_controls(self, frame_id, parent, controls):
+        if frame_id == "actions":
+            buttons = []
+            for control in controls:
+                if control["type"] != "button":
+                    await self._mount_regular_control(parent, control)
+                    continue
+                button = await self._mount_button(parent, control)
+                if button is not None:
+                    buttons.append(button)
+            for offset in range(0, len(buttons), 3):
+                row = Horizontal(classes="action_row")
+                await parent.mount(row)
+                for button in buttons[offset:offset + 3]:
+                    await row.mount(button)
+            return
+
+        index = 0
+        while index < len(controls):
+            control = controls[index]
+            if control["type"] == "progressbar" and control.get("compact"):
+                compact = []
+                while index < len(controls):
+                    candidate = controls[index]
+                    if candidate["type"] != "progressbar" or not candidate.get("compact"):
+                        break
+                    compact.append(candidate)
+                    index += 1
+                row = Horizontal(classes="compact_row")
+                await parent.mount(row)
+                for candidate in compact:
+                    await row.mount(Static(
+                        self._progressbar_text(candidate, compact=True),
+                        classes="compact_progress",
+                    ))
+                continue
+            await self._mount_regular_control(parent, control)
+            index += 1
+
+    async def refresh_screen(self):
+        if self.controller.quit_requested:
+            self.exit()
+            return
+
+        screen_id = self.controller.screen
+        screen = self.screens.get(screen_id)
+        if not screen:
+            self.controller.screen = "front_page"
+            screen = self.screens["front_page"]
+            screen_id = "front_page"
+
+        self._frame_definitions(screen)
+        self.ctx = self.controller.get_context()
+        self._button_actions = {}
+        self._button_seq = 0
+
+        controls_by_frame = {frame_id: [] for frame_id in self.FRAME_ORDER}
+        for control in screen["controls"]:
+            frame_id = control["frame"]
+            if frame_id not in controls_by_frame:
+                raise ValueError(f"Control uses unknown frame {frame_id!r}")
+            controls_by_frame[frame_id].append(control)
+
+        for frame_id in self.FRAME_ORDER:
+            frame = self.query_one(f"#frame_{frame_id}", Vertical)
+            frame.display = bool(controls_by_frame[frame_id])
+            content = self.query_one(f"#{frame_id}_content", (Vertical, VerticalScroll))
+            await content.remove_children()
+            if frame.display:
+                await self._mount_frame_controls(
+                    frame_id,
+                    content,
+                    controls_by_frame[frame_id],
+                )
+
+    async def on_input_submitted(self, event: Input.Submitted):
+        if event.input.id == "name_input":
+            self.controller.set_pending_name(event.value.strip())
+            await self.refresh_screen()
+
+    async def on_button_pressed(self, event: Button.Pressed):
+        action = self._button_actions.get(event.button.id or "")
+        if not action:
+            return
+        if self.controller.screen == "character_creation":
+            name = self.query_one("#name_input", Input).value.strip()
+            self.controller.set_pending_name(name)
+        self.controller.dispatch(action)
+        await self.refresh_screen()
+
+
+def main():
+    HeroAdventureTUI().run()
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()
+

import asyncio
from rich.text import Text
from textual.widgets import Button, Static
from play import HeroAdventureTUI
from hero_engine import HeroAdventureEngine

def text_of(widget):
    if isinstance(widget, Static):
        value = widget.renderable
        return value.plain if isinstance(value, Text) else str(value)
    if isinstance(widget, Button):
        value = widget.label
        return value.plain if isinstance(value, Text) else str(value)
    return ''

async def main():
    app = HeroAdventureTUI()
    async with app.run_test(size=(120, 40)) as pilot:
        app.controller.engine = HeroAdventureEngine('Tester', 'Hitter')
        cases = [
            ('journey', {}, {'status': ['Tester', 'HP:', 'Carry:', 'Leg 1/5'], 'scene': ['Journey events'], 'actions': ['Continue Journey']}),
            ('combat', {'monster_name': 'Goblin'}, {'context': ['Enemy Stats', 'Fight profile', 'Fight', 'Stealth Kill'], 'actions': ['Fight', 'Sneak', 'Steal']}),
            ('inventory', {}, {'context': ['Inventory', 'Your inventory is empty.'], 'actions': ['Character', 'Save Game', 'Close']}),
            ('dungeon_floor_preview', {}, {'context': ['Dungeon', 'Floor monster'], 'scene': ['Dungeon Floor'], 'actions': ['Fight Floor']}),
            ('level_up', {}, {'context': ['Selected', 'Skills'], 'actions': ['Continue']}),
            ('capital', {}, {'context': ['Houses'], 'scene': ['The Capital'], 'actions': ['Keep Pension']}),
        ]
        for screen_id, ctx, expected in cases:
            app.controller.screen = screen_id
            app.controller.ctx = ctx
            await app.refresh_screen(); await pilot.pause()
            print(f'[{screen_id}]')
            for frame_id, wanted in expected.items():
                frame = app.query_one(f'#frame_{frame_id}')
                rendered = ' | '.join(text_of(widget) for widget in frame.query(Static, Button))
                for token in wanted:
                    assert token in rendered, (screen_id, frame_id, token, rendered)
                print(f'  {frame_id}: {rendered[:220]}')

asyncio.run(main())

import asyncio
from rich.text import Text
from textual.widgets import Button, Static
from play import HeroAdventureTUI
from hero_engine import HeroAdventureEngine

def text_of(widget):
    value = widget.content if isinstance(widget, Static) else widget.label
    return value.plain if isinstance(value, Text) else str(value)

async def main():
    app = HeroAdventureTUI()
    async with app.run_test(size=(120, 40)) as pilot:
        app.controller.engine = HeroAdventureEngine('Tester', 'Hitter')
        cases = [
            ('journey', {}, {'status': ['Tester', 'HP:', 'Carry:', 'Leg 1/5'], 'scene': ['Journey events'], 'actions': ['Continue Journey']}),
            ('combat', {'monster_name': 'Goblin'}, {'context': ['Enemy Stats', 'Fight profile', 'Fight', 'Stealth Kill'], 'actions': ['Fight', 'Sneak', 'Steal']}),
            ('inventory', {}, {'context': ['Inventory', 'Your inventory is empty.'], 'actions': ['Character', 'Save Game', 'Close']}),
            ('dungeon_floor_preview', {}, {'context': ['Dungeon', 'Floor monster'], 'scene': ['Dungeon Floor'], 'actions': ['Fight Floor']}),
            ('level_up', {}, {'context': ['Selected', 'Skills'], 'actions': ['Continue']}),
            ('capital', {}, {'context': ['Houses'], 'scene': ['The Capital'], 'actions': ['Keep Pension']}),
        ]
        for screen_id, ctx, expected in cases:
            app.controller.screen = screen_id
            app.controller.ctx = ctx
            await app.refresh_screen(); await pilot.pause()
            print(f'[{screen_id}]')
            for frame_id, wanted in expected.items():
                frame = app.query_one(f'#frame_{frame_id}')
                widgets = list(frame.query(Static)) + list(frame.query(Button))
                rendered = ' | '.join(text_of(widget) for widget in widgets)
                for token in wanted:
                    assert token in rendered, (screen_id, frame_id, token, rendered)
                print(f'  {frame_id}: {rendered[:220]}')

asyncio.run(main())
PY

import asyncio
from rich.text import Text
from textual.widgets import Button, Static
from play import HeroAdventureTUI
from hero_engine import HeroAdventureEngine

def text_of(widget):
    value = widget.content if isinstance(widget, Static) else widget.label
    return value.plain if isinstance(value, Text) else str(value)

def frame_text(app, frame_id):
    frame = app.query_one(f'#frame_{frame_id}')
    widgets = list(frame.query(Static)) + list(frame.query(Button))
    return ' | '.join(text_of(widget) for widget in widgets)

async def main():
    app = HeroAdventureTUI()
    async with app.run_test(size=(120, 40)) as pilot:
        engine = HeroAdventureEngine('Tester', 'Hitter')
        app.controller.engine = engine
        engine.in_dungeon = True
        engine.dungeon_name = "The Goblin's Den"
        engine.dungeon_boss = 'Goblin King'
        engine.dungeon_floors = ['Goblin Scavenger', 'Goblin Sentry', 'Goblin Bruiser', 'Goblin Shaman', 'Goblin Champion']
        cases = [
            ('journey', {}),
            ('combat', None),
            ('inventory', {}),
            ('dungeon_floor_preview', None),
            ('level_up', {}),
            ('capital', {}),
        ]
        for screen_id, ctx in cases:
            if screen_id == 'combat':
                app.controller._start_combat('Goblin', 'journey')
            elif screen_id == 'dungeon_floor_preview':
                app.controller._enter_dungeon_floor_preview()
            else:
                app.controller.screen = screen_id
                app.controller.ctx = ctx
            await app.refresh_screen(); await pilot.pause()
            content = {frame_id: frame_text(app, frame_id) for frame_id in app.FRAME_ORDER}
            unresolved = [token for token in content.values() if '{' in token or '}' in token]
            assert not unresolved, (screen_id, unresolved, content)
            print(f'[{screen_id}]')
            for frame_id in app.FRAME_ORDER:
                frame = app.query_one(f'#frame_{frame_id}')
                if frame.display:
                    print(f'  {frame_id} {frame.region.height}: {content[frame_id][:260]}')
            for frame_id in ('scene', 'context'):
                scroll = app.query_one(f'#{frame_id}_content')
                if scroll.display:
                    print(f'  {frame_id} content={scroll.content_size} viewport={scroll.content_region.size}')

asyncio.run(main())

*** Update File: /home/paul/flutter/copilot-worktrees/gameideas/paul-padataanalytics-laughing-carnival/uigames/hero_adventure/UI_FRAME_PORTING_GUIDE.md
@@
 `frame` is required on every control. The order of controls is the order within its
 frame. The frame declaration is the contract; the renderer owns the geometry.
+
+Controls may also declare `compact: true` when a renderer can safely place several
+small controls on one line. The terminal uses this for the persistent status bars and
+combat odds; a GUI may ignore the hint and give each control its own row.
@@
 `play_gui.py` creates four weighted rows using the 15/50/20/15 default. The ratios do
 not live in widget coordinates in JSON. Empty frames collapse rather than leaving a
 large blank region on menu screens. `scene` and `context` use bounded internal
 content areas; the root window is not one unbounded scrollable document.
+
+`play.py` uses the same four rows. At a 120-column terminal it puts actions in four
+compact columns and renders consecutive compact progressbars on one line. Scene and
+context are bounded scrollable regions; status and actions are fixed and must not
+overflow their frame.
*** End Patch

import asyncio
from pathlib import Path
import json
from play import HeroAdventureTUI
from hero_engine import HeroAdventureEngine

async def prepare(controller, screen_id):
    controller.engine = HeroAdventureEngine('Tester', 'Hitter')
    controller.ctx = {}
    controller.screen = screen_id
    if screen_id == 'character_creation':
        controller.engine = None
    elif screen_id == 'combat':
        controller._start_combat('Goblin', 'journey')
    elif screen_id in {'dungeon_floor_preview', 'dungeon_boss_preview'}:
        e = controller.engine
        e.in_dungeon = True
        e.dungeon_name = "The Goblin's Den"
        e.dungeon_boss = 'Goblin King'
        e.dungeon_floors = ['Goblin Scavenger', 'Goblin Sentry', 'Goblin Bruiser', 'Goblin Shaman', 'Goblin Champion']
        e.dungeon_event_count = 5 if screen_id == 'dungeon_boss_preview' else 0
        controller._enter_dungeon_floor_preview()
    elif screen_id == 'item_detail':
        item = controller.engine.generate_random_item()
        controller.engine.inventory = [item]
        controller.selected_item_letter = 'a'
    elif screen_id == 'wandering_trader':
        controller.trader_offer = [controller.engine.generate_random_item() for _ in range(5)]
    elif screen_id == 'combat_result':
        controller.ctx = {'result_text': 'Victory!', 'combat_rounds': [{'text': 'A hit.', 'action': None, 'enabled': False}]}
    elif screen_id in {'loot_screen', 'magic_shrine_event'}:
        controller.ctx = {'loot_cash': 25, 'loot_lines': [{'text': 'Common Sword', 'action': None, 'enabled': False}], 'loot_items': []}
    elif screen_id == 'capital_result':
        controller.ctx = {'final_house': 'Cottage', 'final_score': 100, 'final_pension': 100}

async def main():
    app = HeroAdventureTUI()
    async with app.run_test(size=(120, 40)) as pilot:
        screen_ids = sorted(app.screens)
        for screen_id in screen_ids:
            await prepare(app.controller, screen_id)
            await app.refresh_screen()
            await pilot.pause()
            frames = [app.query_one(f'#frame_{frame_id}') for frame_id in app.FRAME_ORDER]
            visible = [frame for frame in frames if frame.display]
            assert all(frame.region.y >= 1 and frame.region.bottom <= 39 for frame in visible), screen_id
            assert all(a.region.bottom <= b.region.y for a, b in zip(visible, visible[1:])), screen_id
            for frame_id in ('status', 'actions'):
                frame = app.query_one(f'#frame_{frame_id}')
                if not frame.display:
                    continue
                for child in app.query_one(f'#{frame_id}_content').children:
                    assert child.region.y >= frame.region.y, (screen_id, frame_id, child.region)
                    assert child.region.bottom <= frame.region.bottom, (screen_id, frame_id, child.region, frame.region)
        print(f'Validated {len(screen_ids)} screens at 120x40; fixed-frame children stayed inside bounds')

asyncio.run(main())

You’re right—the implementation preserved the old document-like layout instead of creating visibly distinct information panes.

The agreed default was:

| Frame | Ratio | Priority | Contents |
|---|---:|---|---|
| **Status** | 15% | P0 | Hero identity, HP, gold, carry, journey/dungeon progress, key skills |
| **Scene** | 50% | P0 | Current event, narration, encounter, result, loot, or retirement decision |
| **Context** | 20% | P1 | One supporting mode: combat odds, inventory, dungeon details, trader/capital data, or messages |
| **Actions** | 15% | P0 | Legal actions only: roughly 70% primary, 20% utility, 10% navigation |

These were meant to be four visibly separated, bounded frames—not merely controls tagged with frame names. Under pressure, `context` collapses first; `actions`, `scene`, and `status` remain. On wide screens, context may move beside scene at roughly 25%/75%, but the semantic separation remains.

157.     def __init__(self):
158.         super().__init__()

165.     def _load_screens(self):
166.         ui_dir = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "ui"
167.         screens = {}
168.         for path in ui_dir.glob("*.json"):
169.             data = json.loads(path.read_text())
170.             screens[data["id"]] = data
171.         return screens

173.     def _fmt(self, value):
174.         return str(value).format_map(SafeDict(self.ctx))

176.     def _resolve_number(self, value, control_id, field):
177.         rendered = self._fmt(value)
178.         try:
179.             return float(rendered)
180.         except (TypeError, ValueError) as exc:
181.             raise ValueError(
182.                 f"Invalid progressbar {field} for {control_id}: {rendered!r}"
183.             ) from exc

185.     def _frame_definitions(self, screen):
186.         if len(screen["frames"]) != len(self.FRAME_ORDER):
187.             raise ValueError(f"Screen {screen['id']} must declare exactly four frames")
188.         definitions = {frame["id"]: frame for frame in screen["frames"]}
189.         if set(definitions) != set(self.FRAME_ORDER):
190.             raise ValueError(f"Screen {screen['id']} has invalid frame IDs")
191.         ratio_total = sum(float(definitions[frame_id]["ratio"]) for frame_id in self.FRAME_ORDER)
192.         if abs(ratio_total - 1.0) > 0.001:
193.             raise ValueError(f"Screen {screen['id']} frame ratios must total 1.0")
194.         for frame_id in self.FRAME_ORDER:
195.             frame = definitions[frame_id]
196.             expected_ratio = self.FRAME_WEIGHTS[frame_id] / 100
197.             if frame.get("role") != frame_id or abs(float(frame["ratio"]) - expected_ratio) > 0.001:
198.                 raise ValueError(f"Screen {screen['id']} has invalid {frame_id} frame metadata")
199.         return definitions

201.     def compose(self) -> ComposeResult:
202.         yield Header(show_clock=True)
203.         with Vertical(id="layout"):
204.             with Vertical(id="frame_status", classes="frame"):

206.             with Vertical(id="frame_scene", classes="frame"):
207.                 yield VerticalScroll(id="scene_content", classes="frame_content")
208.             with Vertical(id="frame_context", classes="frame"):
209.                 yield VerticalScroll(id="context_content", classes="frame_content")
210.             with Vertical(id="frame_actions", classes="frame"):
211.                 yield Vertical(id="actions_content", classes="frame_content")
212.         yield Footer()

217.     def _button_id(self, action):

223.     def _progressbar_text(self, control, compact=False):
224.         control_id = control["id"]
225.         value = self._resolve_number(control["value"], control_id, "value")
226.         maximum = self._resolve_number(control["max"], control_id, "max")
227.         if maximum <= 0:
228.             raise ValueError(f"Progressbar {control_id} must have a positive max")
229. 
230.         ratio = value / maximum
231.         display_ratio = min(1.0, max(0.0, ratio))
232.         kind = control.get("kind", "journey")
233.         color = self.BAR_COLORS.get(kind, "cyan")
234.         thresholds = control.get("thresholds", {})
235.         if kind == "health":
236.             if ratio <= thresholds.get("critical", 0.15):
237.                 color = "red"
238.             elif ratio <= thresholds.get("warning", 0.35):
239.                 color = "yellow"
240.         elif kind == "capacity":
241.             if ratio >= thresholds.get("critical", 1.0):
242.                 color = "red"
243.             elif ratio >= thresholds.get("warning", 0.8):
244.                 color = "yellow"
245. 
246.         width = 8 if compact else max(12, min(28, (self.size.width - 34) // 2))
247.         filled = round(display_ratio * width)
248.         bar = "#" * filled + "-" * (width - filled)
249.         label = self._fmt(control.get("label", control_id))
250.         text = Text()
251.         text.append(f"{label:<12} ")
252.         text.append(f"[{bar}]", style=color)
253.         if control.get("show_text", True):
254.             text.append(f" {value:g}/{maximum:g}")
255.         return text

257.     async def _mount_text(self, parent, control, title=False):
258.         value = self._fmt(control.get("value", ""))
259.         if not value and not control.get("show_empty", False):
260.             return
261.         if title:
262.             value = Text(value, style="bold cyan")
263.         await parent.mount(Static(value, classes="line"))

265.     async def _mount_input(self, parent, control):
266.         row = Horizontal(classes="input_row")
267.         await parent.mount(row)
268.         await row.mount(Label(self._fmt(control.get("label", "")), classes="input_label"))
269.         name_input = Input(
270.             placeholder=control.get("placeholder", ""),
271.             id=control.get("id"),
272.         )
273.         name_input.value = self.controller.pending_name
274.         await row.mount(name_input)

276.     async def _mount_list(self, parent, control):
277.         list_id = control["id"]
278.         label = control.get("label")
279.         rows = self.ctx.get(list_id, [])
280.         if label:
281.             await parent.mount(Static(self._fmt(label), classes="list_label"))
282. 
283.         max_rows = control.get("max_rows")
284.         visible_rows = rows[:max_rows] if max_rows else rows
285.         for row in visible_rows:
286.             text = self._fmt(row.get("text", ""))
287.             action = row.get("action")
288.             enabled = row.get("enabled", True)
289.             if action and enabled:
290.                 button_id = self._button_id(action)
291.                 await parent.mount(Button(text, classes="action_button", id=button_id))
292.             else:
293.                 await parent.mount(Static(f"- {text}", classes="disabled_line"))
294. 
295.         if max_rows and len(rows) > max_rows:
296.             await parent.mount(Static(
297.                 f"Showing {max_rows} of {len(rows)} entries; scroll for more.",
298.                 classes="disabled_line",
299.             ))

301.     async def _mount_button(self, parent, control):
302.         visible_if = control.get("visible_if")
303.         if visible_if and not self.ctx.get(visible_if):
304.             return None
305.         label = self._fmt(control.get("label", ""))
306.         action = control.get("action")
307.         if not action:
308.             return Static(f"- {label}", classes="disabled_line")
309.         button_id = self._button_id(action)
310.         return Button(label, classes="action_button", id=button_id)

312.     async def _mount_regular_control(self, parent, control):
313.         control_type = control["type"]
314.         if control_type == "text":
315.             await self._mount_text(parent, control, title=control.get("variant") == "title")
316.         elif control_type == "input":
317.             await self._mount_input(parent, control)
318.         elif control_type == "progressbar":
319.             await parent.mount(Static(
320.                 self._progressbar_text(control),
321.                 classes="progress_line",
322.             ))
323.         elif control_type == "list":
324.             await self._mount_list(parent, control)
325.         else:
326.             raise ValueError(f"Unsupported control type {control_type!r}")
327. 
328.     async def _mount_frame_controls(self, frame_id, parent, controls):
329.         if frame_id == "actions":
330.             buttons = []
331.             for control in controls:
332.                 if control["type"] != "button":
333.                     await self._mount_regular_control(parent, control)
334.                     continue
335.                 button = await self._mount_button(parent, control)
336.                 if button is not None:
337.                     if self.size.width < 100:
338.                         button.add_class("narrow_action")
339.                     buttons.append(button)
340.             columns = 4 if self.size.width >= 80 else 3
341.             for offset in range(0, len(buttons), columns):
342.                 row = Horizontal(classes="action_row")
343.                 if self.size.width < 100:
344.                     row.add_class("narrow_action")
345.                 await parent.mount(row)
346.                 for button in buttons[offset:offset + columns]:
347.                     await row.mount(button)
348.             return
349. 
350.         index = 0
351.         while index < len(controls):
352.             control = controls[index]
353.             if control["type"] == "progressbar" and control.get("compact"):
354.                 compact = []
355.                 while index < len(controls):
356.                     candidate = controls[index]
357.                     if candidate["type"] != "progressbar" or not candidate.get("compact"):
358.                         break
359.                     compact.append(candidate)
360.                     index += 1
361.                 row = Horizontal(classes="compact_row")
362.                 await parent.mount(row)
363.                 for candidate in compact:
364.                     await row.mount(Static(
365.                         self._progressbar_text(candidate, compact=True),
366.                         classes="compact_progress",
367.                     ))
368.                 continue
369.             await self._mount_regular_control(parent, control)
370.             index += 1
371. 
372.     async def refresh_screen(self):
373.         if self.controller.quit_requested:
374.             self.exit()
375.             return
376. 
377.         screen_id = self.controller.screen
378.         screen = self.screens.get(screen_id)
379.         if not screen:
380.             self.controller.screen = "front_page"
381.             screen = self.screens["front_page"]
382.             screen_id = "front_page"
383. 
384.         self._frame_definitions(screen)
385.         self.ctx = self.controller.get_context()
386.         self._button_actions = {}
387.         self._button_seq = 0
388. 
389.         controls_by_frame = {frame_id: [] for frame_id in self.FRAME_ORDER}
390.         for control in screen["controls"]:
391.             frame_id = control["frame"]
392.             if frame_id not in controls_by_frame:
393.                 raise ValueError(f"Control uses unknown frame {frame_id!r}")
394.             controls_by_frame[frame_id].append(control)
395. 
396.         for frame_id in self.FRAME_ORDER:
397.             frame = self.query_one(f"#frame_{frame_id}", Vertical)
398.             frame.display = bool(controls_by_frame[frame_id])
399.             content = self.query_one(f"#{frame_id}_content", (Vertical, VerticalScroll))
400.             await content.remove_children()
401.             if frame.display:
402.                 await self._mount_frame_controls(
403.                     frame_id,
404.                     content,
405.                     controls_by_frame[frame_id],
406.                 )
407. 
408.     async def on_input_submitted(self, event: Input.Submitted):
409.         if event.input.id == "name_input":
410.             self.controller.set_pending_name(event.value.strip())
411.             await self.refresh_screen()
412. 
413.     async def on_button_pressed(self, event: Button.Pressed):
414.         action = self._button_actions.get(event.button.id or "")
415.         if not action:
416.             return
417.         if self.controller.screen == "character_creation":
418.             name = self.query_one("#name_input", Input).value.strip()
419.             self.controller.set_pending_name(name)
420.         self.controller.dispatch(action)

109.             if frame_id not in controls_by_frame:
110.                 raise ValueError(
111.                     f"Control {control.get('id', control.get('type'))} uses unknown frame "
112.                     f"{frame_id!r}"
113.                 )
114.             controls_by_frame[frame_id].append(control)

116.         containers = {}
117.         for row, frame_id in enumerate(self.FRAME_ORDER):
118.             has_controls = bool(controls_by_frame[frame_id])

120.             self.frame.grid_rowconfigure(row, weight=weight, minsize=0)
121.             frame = ctk.CTkFrame(self.frame)

1. # Fixed UI frame design for Hero Adventure
2. 
3. ## Problem and proposed approach
4. 
5. The current JSON describes screens as an ordered list of text, lists, and buttons. Both
6. renderers turn that list into an unbounded vertical document, so long narration, combat
7. logs, inventory rows, and action labels compete for height and produce inconsistent
8. layouts. The next UI contract should describe a small set of semantic frames and typed
9. content slots. A GUI or terminal implementation owns actual dimensions, typography, and
10. whether a frame is visible; the shared JSON owns frame identity, role, content binding,
11. priority, and overflow behavior.
12. 
13. The common contract should support exactly four semantic frames:
14. 
15. - `status`: persistent hero identity, HP, gold, carry weight, journey progress, and
16.   only the most important skill/equipment summary.
17. - `scene`: the current event, narration, encounter, preview, result, loot, or
18.   retirement decision. This is the only frame allowed to own the active situation.
19. - `context`: bounded supporting information such as combat odds, inventory rows,
20.   character detail, trader stock, dungeon depth, house affordability, or recent
21.   messages. It shows one context mode at a time rather than every available fact.
22. - `actions`: currently legal choices, ordered into primary, utility, and navigation
23.   groups with stable action identifiers.
24. 
25. `bars` are typed value/max indicators with a semantic label, thresholds, and optional
26. text fallback. A bar is an amount visualization, never a scrollbar.
27. 
28. Every slot should carry enough metadata for implementations to make safe decisions:
29. `role`, `content_type`, `bind`, `priority`, `visible_if`, and `overflow` (`truncate`,
30. `page`, `collapse`, or `replace`). The base should not contain pixel widths, terminal
31. columns, or GUI coordinates.
32. 
33. ## Information inventory from the current game
34. 
35. The journey is the primary persistent view: leg and route, event 0-20, dungeon count,
36. current narration, HP/max HP, gold, eight effective skills, carry/max weight, equipment,
37. save status, and navigation to character/inventory/save/quit. Combat adds enemy
38. fight/defence/magic, action success percentages and risk bands, projected damage and
39. rounds, plus fight/sneak/steal/stealth-kill/run actions. Other screens add bounded
40. lists:
41. inventory/equipment, character stats, item detail, level-up selections (3), dungeon
42. floor/boss preview, trader buy/sell, loot, house affordability and score, high scores,
43. and short event/result messages.
44. 
45. The current `VerticalScroll`/`CTkScrollableFrame` renderers are the direct source of the
46. problem: they make every JSON line and row a full-width vertical widget. Combat rounds
47. and inventory/trader rows therefore need explicit bounded regions in the new contract.
48. 
49. ## Four-frame contract and allocation
50. 
51. The canonical default is a full-width vertical stack. The percentages are allocation
52. targets, not pixel or terminal dimensions:
53. 
54. | Frame | Default share | Importance | Content budget |
55. | --- | ---: | --- | --- |
56. | `status` | 15% of height | P0: always retain | Hero identity, HP/gold/carry bars, journey/dungeon progress, and up to four key skills. |
57. | `scene` | 50% of height | P0: always retain | One active situation: narration plus encounter, result, loot, or retirement choice. |
58. | `context` | 20% of height | P1: retain when useful | One bounded mode: combat odds, inventory/detail, trader, dungeon, score, or recent messages. |
59. | `actions` | 15% of height | P0: always retain | Legal actions only: approximately 70% primary, 20% utility, 10% navigation. |
60. 
61. The `scene` owns the player's current question ("what is happening?"); `actions` owns
62. the answer ("what can I do?"); `status` owns persistent orientation ("how am I doing?");
63. and `context` owns optional explanation ("what supporting detail do I need?"). This
64. prevents narration, tables, and buttons from competing for the same unstructured list.
65. 
66. When space is constrained, preserve frames in this order: `actions`, `scene`, `status`,
67. then `context` only if it still fits. The first three may be compressed but are not
68. silently removed. `context` may collapse to a command or detail view. When space is
69. wide, `context` may move beside `scene` (target 25% of width) while `scene` receives
70. 75%; the semantic frame IDs and content budgets do not change.
71. 
72. `context` must use a single active mode:
73. 
74. - Journey/combat: combat odds and the most relevant enemy facts.
75. - Inventory/character: capacity, equipment, or one selected item.
76. - Dungeon: floor/depth and next threat.
77. - Trader/capital: prices, affordability, pension, or score.
78. - Results/events: a bounded recent-message window, with older text paged or opened.
79. 
80. This gives every implementation the same four decisions while allowing terminal and
81. GUI ports to stack, split, collapse, or omit the context presentation.
82. 
83. ## Bar vocabulary
84. 
85. Bars should be declarative records, for example:
86. 
87. ```json
88. {
89.   "id": "hp",
90.   "label": "HP",
91.   "value": "{hp}",
92.   "max": "{max_hp}",
93.   "kind": "health",
94.   "thresholds": {"warning": 0.35, "critical": 0.15},
95.   "show_text": true
96. }
97. ```
98. 
99. Recommended initial bars:
100. 
101. - `hp`: health/max health; critical and warning thresholds.
102. - `carry`: total weight/max weight; warning near capacity and critical when
103.   overburdened.
104. - `journey`: event/20, or a normalized five-leg journey progress value.
105. - `dungeon`: current floor/6 when inside a dungeon.
106. - `level_up`: selected/3 during level-up.
107. - `honor`: honor marks/15 on character detail, not necessarily persistent HUD.
108. - Combat action odds can use small comparative bars, but only in the combat context
109.   block; they should not replace the clear percentage text.
110. 
111. Cash, score, and house affordability are better represented as labeled values or
112. comparative progress against the selected house cost, because their upper bound is
113. screen-dependent.
114. 
115. ## Recommended shared JSON shape
116. 
117. The later implementation should migrate from `text`/`lists`/`buttons` to a structure
118. similar to:
119. 
120. ```json
121. {
122.   "id": "journey",
123.   "frames": [
124.     {"id": "status", "role": "status", "priority": "P0",
125.      "content": ["hero", "bars", "key_skills"]},
126.     {"id": "scene", "role": "scene", "priority": "P0",
127.      "content": ["narration", "active_situation"]},
128.     {"id": "context", "role": "context", "priority": "P1",
129.      "content": ["active_context"], "overflow": "page"},
130.     {"id": "actions", "role": "actions", "priority": "P0",
131.      "content": ["primary_actions", "utility", "navigation"]}
132.   ]
133. }
134. ```
135. 
136. This is a semantic contract, not a mandate that every implementation render four
137. rectangles in the same geometry. A port may stack or split them, and may collapse the
138. `context` frame, but it must preserve the four roles and their priority rules.
139. 
140. ## Current implementation plan: GUI-first frame migration
141. 
142. This phase deliberately makes a one-way migration. The old `text`/`lists`/`buttons`
143. shape will not be supported and no compatibility adapter will be added. The terminal
144. renderer is a later port and will be expected to consume the new contract.
145. 
146. 1. Define the new screen schema in the UI JSON:
147.    - `frames` declares the four roles and their ratio/priority metadata.
148.    - `controls` is a single ordered collection; every control explicitly declares
149.      `frame`, `type`, and its content binding.
150.    - Use `type: "text"`, `type: "list"`, `type: "button"`, `type: "input"`, and
151.      `type: "progressbar"` rather than implicit top-level arrays.
152.    - `progressbar` controls bind `value` and `max`, expose `kind`, thresholds, and
153.      `show_text`, and remain distinct from scrolling.
154. 2. Migrate all `ui/*.json` screens to the new shape. Put persistent HP, carry, and
155.    journey/dungeon progress bars in `status`; narration and the active event in
156.    `scene`; one bounded list/detail/message mode in `context`; and all choices in
